problem: Prior R2R VLN transformers use only RGB of each candidate view independently (no geometry, no local spatial context), and plain cross-attention poorly models how different instruction phrases relate to different visual cues.
motivation: RGB-only inputs bias toward color/texture and overfit training scenes, hurting generalization to unseen environments. Candidate views at a viewpoint can be few, so neighboring views provide needed context. Instruction phrases (e.g. 'go through the corridor' vs 'pick up the spoon') need different modalities.
key_idea: Enrich RGB candidate features with neighbor-view information via local-aware slot attention, fuse them with Omnidata-predicted depth and normal CLIP features, and decide via a multiway attention that weights per-modality matching scores.
insight: Depth or normal alone do not help (baseline RGB+dep or RGB+nor is no better than RGB), but both together help, and LSA gives about +2.5 SPL on val-unseen (58.35 to 60.78 with RGB only is 59.78; full 61.00). Aggregating RGB neighbors first and then fusing depth/normal in a second stage beats variants that apply slot attention to depth/normal or to multimodal neighbors (TwoSM-1/2/3 all worse), indicating misaligned modalities hurt slot aggregation.
method: Geometry inputs: 36-view RGB plus depth and surface-normal maps predicted by off-the-shelf Omnidata (no extra training data), all encoded by frozen CLIP-RN50x4 (640-d) and concatenated with angle features.

Local-aware slot attention: slots initialized from RGB candidate features act as queries; keys/values are the panoramic RGB views; softmax over slot axis, 3 iterations with GRU plus residual MLP; attention mask restricts to views within 30° heading/elevation; residual added to candidate feature.
Two-stage fusion: slot-enhanced RGB, depth, normal and angle features are concatenated and projected by FC+LN to 768-d visual tokens.
Recurrent VLN-BERT backbone: state vector s_t updated recurrently over instruction and geometry-enhanced tokens.

Multiway attention: separate attention scores of s_t with RGB, depth and normal features, combined by softmax modality weights predicted from s_t (matching score), giving K+1 action logits incl. STOP.
Training: IL (teacher forcing) plus A2C RL as in Recurrent VLN-BERT, with augmented data at 1:1; also ported to HAMT (GeoVLN†) using [CLS]-based state vector.

setting.backbone: Recurrent VLN-BERT (GeoVLN) / HAMT (GeoVLN†) with frozen CLIP-RN50x4 encoder and Omnidata predictors
setting.training_data: R2R train plus R2R augmented data (1:1 mix, as in Recurrent VLN-BERT); depth/normal from pretrained Omnidata, no additional training data
setting.observation: 36-view perspective RGB plus predicted depth and normal maps (panoramic, discrete)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph candidate viewpoints plus STOP

numbers_note: Table 1 reports integer SR/SPL; the ablation gives two decimals. Val-seen ablation full: SR 69.64, SPL 64.86.
results: On R2R val-unseen GeoVLN reaches SR 67 / SPL 61 vs its base Recurrent VLN-BERT 63/57, and GeoVLN† (HAMT) reaches 68/63 vs HAMT 66/61. On test-unseen, GeoVLN† gets SR 65 / SPL 61 (HAMT 65/60); val-seen is slightly worse than RecBERT for the base variant.
limitations: Gains are small on test-unseen (SR equal to HAMT) and val-seen performance drops for the RecBERT variant.
Extra compute: memory and inference time up (e.g. 108s vs 70s; GeoVLN† 15.1 GiB vs HAMT 9.9 GiB), and depth/normal are noisy predictions.
Evaluated only on R2R discrete; failure cases include not stopping at stairs.
